## Understanding Supercomputing and Researcher Demand

::: {style="margin-top: 30px;"}

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 0 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
What is Supercomputing (HPC)?
</div>

High-performance computing (HPC) uses **many processors working together** to solve complex problems, run simulations, and analyse large datasets at a scale that ordinary computers cannot easily achieve.

**What makes it different?** Supercomputers combine thousands of CPU cores, often supported by GPUs, to perform calculations **in parallel**.

**Research applications:** Climate modelling, weather forecasting, drug discovery, and engineering simulations.

<div style="height: 10px;"></div>

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 12px 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
Understanding Researcher Demand
</div>

- [**Demand (Requested)**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: Computing resources researchers **request** for their research.
- [**Allocated**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: Computing resources facilities **provide** to researchers.
- [**Unmet demand**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: The portion of requests **not fulfilled**, when the measures are comparable.

::: {style="margin-top: 10px; padding: 8px 14px; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; background-color: #F2F7FB; font-size: 0.85em;"}

**Important:** Historical demand is not always directly observed. Some values are estimated using allocations or proxies, so the forecasts represent **planning scenarios rather than exact predictions**.

:::

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.48em; color: #666; margin-top: 8px;"}

Source: [@ibm_hpc; @NCMAS2026]

:::

## Data Sources and Historical Coverage

::: {style="margin-top: 30px;"}

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 0 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
Primary Data Sources
</div>

- [**NCI**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: National Computational Infrastructure. Historical reports and computing allocations.
- [**Pawsey**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: Pawsey Supercomputing Research Centre. Historical reports and computing allocations.
- [**NCMAS**]{style="color: #006DAE;"}: National Computational Merit Allocation Scheme. Annual allocation outcomes.

<div style="height: 10px;"></div>

<div style="background-color: #EAF3F9; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; padding: 4px 12px; margin: 12px 0 10px 0; color: #005B91; font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em; line-height: 1.1;">
Historical Data Coverage
</div>

- **Overall HPC:** 2014 - 2026, in thousands of service units (**kSU**).
- **CPU:** 2014 - 2026, in million CPU core-hours.
- **GPU:** 2022 - 2026, in million GPU-hours.
- **Fields of Research (FoR):** 2014 - 2026, historical research-field **allocation shares**, not directly observed FoR demand.

<div style="height: 10px;"></div>

::: {style="padding: 8px 14px; border-left: 5px solid #006DAE; background-color: #F2F7FB; font-size: 0.85em;"}

**Data limitation:** Historical series combine reported observations, derived estimates, and proxies. Data availability and comparability vary across facilities and years.

:::

:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.48em; color: #666; margin-top: 8px;"}

Sources: [@NCI201314; @NCIAllocations202021; @Pawsey201617; @NCMAS2026]. Coverage and harmonisation: this project's data preparation methodology.

:::

<div class="prov-panel">
<strong>What does this show?</strong>
<ul>
<li>Allocation is predominantly based on reported awards.</li>
<li>Demand more frequently requires reconstruction from historical information.</li>
<li>Even directly reported values may require harmonisation across facilities and years.</li>
</ul>
</div>

<div class="prov-panel" style="margin-top:11px; background:#FFF5EB;">
<strong>Main limitations</strong>
<ul>
<li>Different service-unit definitions and accounting conventions.</li>
<li>Changes in facility coverage and reporting scope.</li>
<li>Some demand estimates depend on approximate fulfilment relationships.</li>
<li>Incomplete historical CPU/GPU separation.</li>
</ul>
</div>

</div>
</div>

<div class="prov-takeaway">
<strong>Key takeaway:</strong>
Historical demand relies more heavily on reconstructed values than allocation. Transparent assumptions, consistent definitions and improved national data integration are therefore essential for interpreting forecasts and strengthening future HPC planning.
</div>

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 3.3
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: center

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# Load harmonised historical dataset
annual_converted <- readRDS(
  "../assets/data/data converted/annual_demand_allocation_converted.rds"
)

# Load original GPU historical scenarios
historical_gpu_scenarios <- readRDS(
  "../assets/data/data converted/historical_gpu_scenarios.rds"
)

# Verify scenario coverage
stopifnot(
  nrow(historical_gpu_scenarios) == 8,
  identical(
    sort(as.integer(historical_gpu_scenarios$year)),
    2014:2021
  )
)

# Prepare historical series
historical_plot <- annual_converted |>
  transmute(
    year = as.integer(year),

    `Overall HPC|Demand` = demand_ksu / 1e6,
    `Overall HPC|Allocation` = allocation_ksu / 1e6,

    `CPU|Demand` = demand_cpu_core_hours / 1e6,
    `CPU|Allocation` = allocation_cpu_core_hours / 1e6,

    `GPU|Demand` = demand_gpu_hours / 1e6,
    `GPU|Allocation` = allocation_gpu_hours / 1e6
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -year,
    names_to = c("resource", "measure"),
    names_sep = "\\|",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(
    resource = factor(
      resource,
      levels = c("Overall HPC", "CPU", "GPU"),
      labels = c(
        "Overall HPC (million kSU)",
        "CPU (million core-hours)",
        "GPU (million GPU-hours)"
      )
    ),
    measure = factor(
      measure,
      levels = c("Demand", "Allocation")
    )
  )

# Prepare GPU low/high scenario bands, 2014–2021
gpu_uncertainty_data <- historical_gpu_scenarios |>
  select(
    year,
    demand_gpu_hours_low,
    demand_gpu_hours_high,
    allocation_gpu_hours_low,
    allocation_gpu_hours_high
  ) |>
  filter(
    year >= 2014,
    year <= 2021
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -year,
    names_to = c("measure", ".value"),
    names_pattern =
      "(demand|allocation)_(gpu_hours_low|gpu_hours_high)"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    measure = recode(
      measure,
      demand = "Demand",
      allocation = "Allocation"
    ),
    measure = factor(
      measure,
      levels = c("Demand", "Allocation")
    ),
    resource = factor(
      "GPU (million GPU-hours)",
      levels = levels(historical_plot$resource)
    ),
    gpu_hours_low = gpu_hours_low / 1e6,
    gpu_hours_high = gpu_hours_high / 1e6
  )

# Create historical demand and allocation chart
ggplot() +

  # GPU scenario bands, 2014–2021
  geom_ribbon(
    data = gpu_uncertainty_data,
    aes(
      x = year,
      ymin = gpu_hours_low,
      ymax = gpu_hours_high,
      fill = measure,
      group = measure
    ),
    alpha = 0.18,
    colour = NA
  ) +

  # Solid lines:
  # All HPC and CPU years, plus GPU 2022–2026
  geom_line(
    data = historical_plot |>
      filter(
        resource != "GPU (million GPU-hours)" |
          year >= 2022
      ),
    aes(
      x = year,
      y = value,
      colour = measure,
      group = interaction(resource, measure)
    ),
    linewidth = 1.15
  ) +

  # Dashed GPU scenarios, 2014–2021
  geom_line(
    data = historical_plot |>
      filter(
        resource == "GPU (million GPU-hours)",
        year <= 2021
      ),
    aes(
      x = year,
      y = value,
      colour = measure,
      group = measure
    ),
    linewidth = 1.15,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  # Connect scenario period to 2022
  geom_line(
    data = historical_plot |>
      filter(
        resource == "GPU (million GPU-hours)",
        year %in% c(2021, 2022)
      ),
    aes(
      x = year,
      y = value,
      group = measure
    ),
    colour = "#999999",
    linewidth = 0.9,
    linetype = "dotted"
  ) +

  # Demand and allocation observations
  geom_point(
    data = historical_plot,
    aes(
      x = year,
      y = value,
      colour = measure
    ),
    size = 1.8
  ) +

  # GPU scenario / usable-data boundary
  geom_vline(
    data = data.frame(
      resource = factor(
        "GPU (million GPU-hours)",
        levels = levels(historical_plot$resource)
      ),
      boundary = 2021.5
    ),
    aes(xintercept = boundary),
    linetype = "dotted",
    colour = "#888888",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +

  # Resource panels
  facet_wrap(
    ~resource,
    nrow = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "Demand" = "#006DAE",
      "Allocation" = "#E69F00"
    )
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Demand" = "#006DAE",
      "Allocation" = "#E69F00"
    )
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(2014, 2017, 2020, 2023, 2026)
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = NULL,
    colour = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  ) +

  guides(fill = "none") +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +

  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 14,
      face = "bold",
      colour = "#17324D"
    ),
    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "#EAF2F9",
      colour = NA
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 10
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.key.width = grid::unit(1.3, "cm"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(1, "lines"),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 8, 2, 8)
  )
```

<div class="slide7-insights">

<div class="slide7-insight">

<strong>Overall HPC</strong>

<p>
<span class="period">2023 - 2026:</span>
Official NCMAS requests increased
<strong>68%</strong>, while available
resources grew only <strong>6%</strong>.
</p>

<p>
<span class="period">2026:</span>
Oversubscription reached <strong>2.69×</strong>.
Reconstructed growth of <strong>43.3%</strong>
is sensitive to the estimated 2025 baseline.
</p>

</div>

<div class="slide7-insight">

<strong>CPU</strong>

<p>
<span class="period">2019 - 2020:</span>
Raijin transitioned to Gadi, coinciding
with a sharp decline in reconstructed
CPU demand.
</p>

<p>
<span class="period">2022 - 2023:</span>
Magnus transitioned to Setonix.
Infrastructure and accounting changes
may affect historical comparability.
</p>

</div>

<div class="slide7-insight">

<strong>GPU</strong>

<p>
<span class="period">2022 - 2023:</span>
Setonix deployment introduced new
CPU/GPU infrastructure and
allocation arrangements.
</p>

<p>
<span class="period">2023 - 2026:</span>
Official Setonix GPU requests increased
<strong>123%</strong> in kSU.
GPU-hour trends remain less reliable.
</p>

</div>

</div>

<div class="slide7-note">
<strong>Interpretation:</strong>
System transitions may affect historical
comparability but are not confirmed causes
of changes in researcher demand.
GPU values for 2014 - 2021 are assumption-based
historical scenarios, not statistical confidence
intervals. Historical series include reported
and estimated values. The 2025 HPC estimate
affects reconstructed 2026 growth.
The 2026 HPC allocation excludes 12,000 kSU
for Setonix Q. Panel units and scales differ.
</div>

#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| include: false

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(stringr)

# Load historical FoR data
for_converted <- readRDS(
  "../assets/data/data converted/field_of_research_converted.rds"
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(for_converted) == 133,
  identical(
    sort(unique(as.integer(for_converted$year))),
    2014:2026
  )
)

# Consistent colours
for_palette <- c(
  "Physical Sciences" = "#006DAE",
  "Chemical Sciences" = "#38A6D8",
  "Earth & Environmental Sciences" = "#279A8B",
  "Engineering & Technology" = "#E69F00",
  "Biological & Agricultural Sciences" = "#74B86A",
  "Medical & Health Sciences" = "#B77DBD",
  "Mathematics & Computing" = "#E27B66",
  "Social Sciences, Humanities & Built Environment" = "#8B91A9",
  "Unclassified & Operational" = "#B7BEC7"
)

field_order <- names(for_palette)

# ----------------------------------------
# Overall: harmonised groups, 2014–2026
# ----------------------------------------

for_overall <- for_converted |>
  mutate(
    reported_clean = research_field_reported |>
      str_remove("^\\s*\\d{2}\\s+") |>
      str_to_lower() |>
      str_replace_all("&", " and ") |>
      str_squish(),

    field = case_when(
      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "physical sciences|radioastronomy|radio astronomy"
      ) ~ "Physical Sciences",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "chemical sciences"
      ) ~ "Chemical Sciences",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "earth|environmental|geoscien"
      ) ~ "Earth & Environmental Sciences",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "engineering|technology"
      ) ~ "Engineering & Technology",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "biological|agricultural|veterinary|food sciences"
      ) ~ "Biological & Agricultural Sciences",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "medical|health|biomedical|clinical"
      ) ~ "Medical & Health Sciences",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "mathematical|computing|information"
      ) ~ "Mathematics & Computing",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        paste0(
          "psychology|economics|history|archaeology|",
          "human society|language|communication|culture|",
          "philosophy|religious|built environment|design"
        )
      ) ~ "Social Sciences, Humanities & Built Environment",

      str_detect(
        reported_clean,
        "other|unreported|unclassified|pawsey operations"
      ) ~ "Unclassified & Operational",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

stopifnot(
  !anyNA(for_overall$field),
  n_distinct(for_overall$field) == 9
)

for_overall_plot <- for_overall |>
  group_by(year, field) |>
  summarise(
    allocation_share = sum(allocation_share_for),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ----------------------------------------
# Early period: FoR 2008, 2014–2020
# ----------------------------------------

for_early <- for_converted |>
  filter(between(year, 2014, 2020)) |>
  mutate(
    field = case_when(
      for_2008_division_code == "01" ~
        "Mathematics & Computing",

      for_2008_division_code == "02" ~
        "Physical Sciences",

      for_2008_division_code == "03" ~
        "Chemical Sciences",

      for_2008_division_code %in% c(
        "04", "05", "04 + 05"
      ) ~ "Earth & Environmental Sciences",

      for_2008_division_code %in% c(
        "06", "07"
      ) ~ "Biological & Agricultural Sciences",

      for_2008_division_code == "08" ~
        "Mathematics & Computing",

      for_2008_division_code %in% c(
        "09", "10", "09 + 10"
      ) ~ "Engineering & Technology",

      for_2008_division_code == "11" ~
        "Medical & Health Sciences",

      for_2008_division_code %in% c(
        "12", "21"
      ) ~ "Social Sciences, Humanities & Built Environment",

      is.na(for_2008_division_code) ~
        "Unclassified & Operational",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

stopifnot(!anyNA(for_early$field))

for_early_plot <- for_early |>
  group_by(year, field) |>
  summarise(
    allocation_share = sum(allocation_share_for),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ----------------------------------------
# Later period: FoR 2020, 2021–2026
# ----------------------------------------

for_late <- for_converted |>
  filter(between(year, 2021, 2026)) |>
  mutate(
    field = case_when(
      for_standard_2020 %in% c(
        "Engineering",
        "Engineering + Technology",
        "Technology — no direct FoR 2020 alignment"
      ) ~ "Engineering & Technology",

      for_standard_2020 == "Physical sciences" ~
        "Physical Sciences",

      for_standard_2020 == "Chemical sciences" ~
        "Chemical Sciences",

      for_standard_2020 %in% c(
        "Earth sciences",
        "Environmental sciences",
        "Earth sciences + Environmental sciences"
      ) ~ "Earth & Environmental Sciences",

      for_standard_2020 %in% c(
        "Biological sciences",
        "Agricultural, veterinary and food sciences"
      ) ~ "Biological & Agricultural Sciences",

      for_standard_2020 %in% c(
        "Biomedical and clinical sciences",
        "Health sciences",
        "Biomedical and clinical sciences + Health sciences"
      ) ~ "Medical & Health Sciences",

      for_standard_2020 %in% c(
        "Mathematical sciences",
        "Information and computing sciences"
      ) ~ "Mathematics & Computing",

      for_standard_2020 %in% c(
        "Psychology",
        "Economics",
        "History, heritage and archaeology",
        "Language, communication and culture",
        "Philosophy and religious studies",
        "Human society",
        "Built environment and design"
      ) ~ "Social Sciences, Humanities & Built Environment",

      for_standard_2020 == "Other / Unclassified" ~
        "Unclassified & Operational",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

stopifnot(!anyNA(for_late$field))

for_late_plot <- for_late |>
  group_by(year, field) |>
  summarise(
    allocation_share = sum(allocation_share_for),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Validate annual shares before plotting
for (dataset in list(
  for_overall_plot,
  for_early_plot,
  for_late_plot
)) {
  totals <- dataset |>
    group_by(year) |>
    summarise(
      total = sum(allocation_share),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  stopifnot(
    all(abs(totals$total - 1) < 1e-6)
  )
}

# Include absent categories as zero
prepare_for <- function(data) {
  data |>
    mutate(
      field = factor(field, levels = field_order)
    ) |>
    complete(
      year,
      field,
      fill = list(allocation_share = 0)
    )
}

for_overall_plot <- prepare_for(for_overall_plot)
for_early_plot <- prepare_for(for_early_plot)
for_late_plot <- prepare_for(for_late_plot)

# Average annual allocation shares
for_early_average <- for_early_plot |>
  group_by(field) |>
  summarise(
    mean_share = mean(allocation_share),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

for_late_average <- for_late_plot |>
  group_by(field) |>
  summarise(
    mean_share = mean(allocation_share),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Annual leading field
for_top_overall <- for_overall_plot |>
  arrange(year, field) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(
    ymid = cumsum(allocation_share) -
      allocation_share / 2
  ) |>
  slice_max(
    allocation_share,
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    label = percent(
      allocation_share,
      accuracy = 1
    )
  )

# Short labels for average-share charts
short_field_labels <- c(
  "Physical Sciences" = "Physical Sciences",
  "Chemical Sciences" = "Chemical Sciences",
  "Earth & Environmental Sciences" = "Earth & Environmental",
  "Engineering & Technology" = "Engineering & Technology",
  "Biological & Agricultural Sciences" = "Biological & Agricultural",
  "Medical & Health Sciences" = "Medical & Health",
  "Mathematics & Computing" = "Mathematics & Computing",
  "Social Sciences, Humanities & Built Environment" =
    "Social Sciences & Humanities",
  "Unclassified & Operational" =
    "Unclassified & Operational"
)

# ----------------------------------------
# Annual composition chart
# ----------------------------------------

plot_for_overall <- function(data) {
  ggplot(
    data,
    aes(
      x = factor(year),
      y = allocation_share,
      fill = field
    )
  ) +
    geom_col(
      width = 0.83,
      position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)
    ) +
    geom_text(
      data = for_top_overall,
      aes(
        x = factor(year),
        y = ymid,
        label = label
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      colour = "white",
      fontface = "bold",
      size = 3
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = for_palette,
      limits = field_order,
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = label_percent(),
      breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL,
      fill = NULL
    ) +
    guides(
      fill = guide_legend(
        ncol = 3,
        byrow = TRUE
      )
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
      legend.key.size = grid::unit(0.3, "cm"),
      legend.spacing.y = grid::unit(0.05, "cm"),
      plot.margin = margin(3, 6, 2, 6)
    )
}

# ----------------------------------------
# Period-average charts
# ----------------------------------------

plot_for_average <- function(data) {
  chart_data <- data |>
    arrange(mean_share) |>
    mutate(
      field_label = unname(
        short_field_labels[as.character(field)]
      ),
      field_label = factor(
        field_label,
        levels = field_label
      )
    )

  ggplot(
    chart_data,
    aes(
      x = mean_share,
      y = field_label,
      fill = field
    )
  ) +
    geom_col(width = 0.68) +
    geom_text(
      aes(
        label = percent(
          mean_share,
          accuracy = 1
        )
      ),
      hjust = -0.15,
      size = 2.8,
      colour = "#17324D",
      fontface = "bold"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = for_palette,
      guide = "none"
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = label_percent(),
      breaks = seq(0, 0.5, 0.1),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.margin = margin(3, 12, 2, 3)
    )
}

engineering projects, including turbine
and fluid-flow simulations.

requires project-level verification.

</div>

different 2017 Pawsey reporting scope
limit direct interpretation as a change

::: {.slide9}

::: {.slide9-intro}
**Model rationale:** Annual demand data contain **13 observations for HPC and CPU (2014 - 2026)** and **5 for GPU (2022 - 2026)**. Four simple models were compared to test different growth assumptions while limiting model complexity.
:::

::: {.slide9-models}

::: {.slide9-model}
**Naïve benchmark: No growth**

::: {.slide9-equation}
$\hat{D}_{T+h}=D_T$
:::

Future demand remains at the **latest observed level**.
:::

::: {.slide9-model}
**Drift benchmark: Historical average growth**

::: {.slide9-equation}
$\hat{D}_{T+h}=D_T+h\frac{D_T-D_1}{T-1}$
:::

Extends the **average annual change** from the first to last observation.
:::

::: {.slide9-model}
**Linear trend: Absolute growth**

::: {.slide9-equation}
$D_t=\alpha+\beta t+\varepsilon_t$
:::

Estimates a **constant annual change** using all observations.
:::

::: {.slide9-model}
**Log-linear trend: Proportional growth**

::: {.slide9-equation}
$\log(D_t)=\alpha+\beta t+\varepsilon_t$
:::

Estimates a **constant percentage growth rate**.
:::

:::

::: {.slide9-section}
Sensitivity analysis: Influence of 2026
:::

::: {.slide9-reason}
The reconstructed demand rises sharply in 2026. Linear trends were fitted **with and without 2026** to assess the effect on estimated annual growth.
:::

| Resource | Excluding 2026 | Including 2026 | Change |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| **Overall HPC** | 144,357 kSU/year | **161,992 kSU/year** | **+12.2%** |
| **CPU** | 72.41M core-hours/year | **81.01M core-hours/year** | **+11.9%** |
| **GPU** | 0.012M GPU-hours/year | **0.172M GPU-hours/year** | Highly sensitive |

::: {.slide9-finding}
**Key finding:** Including 2026 increases the fitted linear growth rate by approximately **12% for HPC and CPU**. GPU growth estimates are particularly unstable because only five annual observations are available.
:::

::: {.slide9-for}
**Field of Research:** Historical allocation shares inform FoR scenarios; separate FoR demand regressions were not fitted because directly observed field-level demand series are unavailable.
:::

::: {.slide9-note}
**Notes:** GPU models use 2022 - 2026 observations, excluding assumption-based 2014 - 2021 scenarios. Sensitivity measures changes in fitted slopes, not forecast accuracy.
:::

::: {style="font-size: 10px; color: #666; margin-top: 5px; line-height: 1.15;"}
**Methods:** Naïve and drift benchmarks, linear and log-linear regression [@HyndmanAthanasopoulos2021, Chapters 5 and 7]. Sensitivity results: project calculations.
:::

:::

::: {.slide10}

::: {.slide10-intro}
**Evaluation approach:** The four models introduced previously were assessed using **expanding-window, one-step-ahead cross-validation** to compare their predictive performance on historical observations.
:::

::: {.slide10-method}
**How it works:** Fit each model using the available earlier years, predict the next year, then expand the training window and repeat.

**Accuracy measures:** **RMSE** gives greater weight to large forecast errors; **MAE** measures the average absolute error. Lower values indicate better performance.
:::

::: {.slide10-chart}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 3.65
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: center

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

accuracy_data <- data.frame(
  resource = rep(
    c("Overall HPC", "CPU", "GPU"),
    each = 4
  ),
  model = rep(
    c("Naïve", "Drift", "Linear", "Log-linear"),
    times = 3
  ),
  RMSE = c(
    378864, 314588, 290898, 511614,
    260.05, 242.61, 157.72, 160.18,
    0.441, 0.537, 0.729, 0.719
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    resource = factor(
      resource,
      levels = c("Overall HPC", "CPU", "GPU"),
      labels = c(
        "Overall HPC (thousand kSU)",
        "CPU (million core-hours)",
        "GPU (million GPU-hours)"
      )
    ),
    model = factor(
      model,
      levels = c("Naïve", "Drift", "Linear", "Log-linear")
    ),
    plot_rmse = if_else(
      resource == "Overall HPC (thousand kSU)",
      RMSE / 1000,
      RMSE
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(resource) |>
  mutate(
    best = plot_rmse == min(plot_rmse),
    label = if_else(
      resource == "Overall HPC (thousand kSU)",
      sprintf("%.1f", plot_rmse),
      sprintf("%.2f", plot_rmse)
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(
  accuracy_data,
  aes(x = model, y = plot_rmse, fill = best)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = label),
    vjust = -0.45,
    size = 4,
    fontface = "bold",
    colour = "#17324D"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ resource,
    nrow = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "TRUE" = "#006DAE",
      "FALSE" = "#A9CDE3"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.17))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Cross-validation RMSE"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 13,
      face = "bold",
      colour = "#17324D"
    ),
    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "#EAF3F9",
      colour = NA
    ),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      size = 10,
      angle = 30,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.2, "lines"),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 12, 5, 5)
  )
```
:::

<div class="slide10-findings">

<div class="slide10-finding">
<strong>Overall HPC</strong>
<p><strong>Linear</strong> achieved the lowest RMSE of <strong>290,898 kSU</strong> and MAE of <strong>198,295 kSU</strong>.</p>
<p>Six evaluation years: 2021–2026.</p>
</div>

<div class="slide10-finding">
<strong>CPU</strong>
<p><strong>Linear</strong> had the lowest RMSE at <strong>157.72 million core-hours</strong>.</p>
<p><strong>Log-linear</strong> had the lowest MAE at <strong>133.74 million core-hours</strong>.</p>
</div>

<div class="slide10-finding">
<strong>GPU</strong>
<p><strong>Naïve</strong> had the lowest RMSE at <strong>0.441 million GPU-hours</strong>.</p>
<p>Only two evaluation years (2025–2026), so model rankings are highly uncertain.</p>
</div>

</div>

::: {.slide10-conclusion}
**Key finding:** Linear trends had the lowest one-step-ahead RMSE for **overall HPC and CPU**, while naïve performed best for **GPU**. These results guide model selection but do not establish accuracy for forecasts through 2030.
:::

::: {.slide10-note}
**Notes:** Chart shows RMSE, not MAE. Units are thousand kSU for HPC and million hours for CPU/GPU; panel scales differ. HPC/CPU use six one-step-ahead errors; GPU uses two. **Methods:** [@HyndmanAthanasopoulos2021, Chapter 5]. **Results:** Project model evaluation.
:::

::: {.slide11-heading}
Residual diagnostics for selected linear models
:::

::: {.slide11-chart}

```{r}
#| label: slide11-residual-diagnostics
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.0
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: center

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# -------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Locate the repository root reproducibly
# -------------------------------------------------------

# The here package uses project-root markers such as
# an .Rproj file, .here file, or Git repository.

if (!requireNamespace("here", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop(
    "The 'here' package is required. ",
    "Install it with install.packages('here')."
  )
}

project_root <- here::here()

hpc_path <- here::here(
  "assets",
  "models",
  "overall_hpc_models.rds"
)

cpu_path <- here::here(
  "assets",
  "models",
  "cpu_models.rds"
)

# Check that here() has identified the correct project.
if (!file.exists(hpc_path) || !file.exists(cpu_path)) {
  stop(
    "Saved model files were not found.\n",
    "Project root detected: ", project_root, "\n",
    "Expected HPC file: ", hpc_path, "\n",
    "Expected CPU file: ", cpu_path, "\n",
    "Check the project root and assets/models folder."
  )
}

# -------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load the original fitted forecasting models
# -------------------------------------------------------

hpc_models <- readRDS(hpc_path)
cpu_models <- readRDS(cpu_path)

overall_linear <- hpc_models$overall_linear
cpu_linear <- cpu_models$cpu_linear

if (!inherits(overall_linear, "lm") ||
    !inherits(cpu_linear, "lm")) {
  stop(
    "The saved files must contain the fitted ",
    "overall_linear and cpu_linear lm objects."
  )
}

# -------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Extract residuals
# -------------------------------------------------------

hpc_residuals <- as.numeric(
  residuals(overall_linear)
)

cpu_residuals <- as.numeric(
  residuals(cpu_linear)
)

stopifnot(
  length(hpc_residuals) >= 3,
  length(cpu_residuals) >= 3,
  all(is.finite(hpc_residuals)),
  all(is.finite(cpu_residuals))
)

# -------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Recalculate Ljung-Box tests
# -------------------------------------------------------

# Match the diagnostic specification in the report:
# lag = 2, fitdf = 0.

hpc_lb <- Box.test(
  hpc_residuals,
  lag = 2,
  type = "Ljung-Box",
  fitdf = 0
)

cpu_lb <- Box.test(
  cpu_residuals,
  lag = 2,
  type = "Ljung-Box",
  fitdf = 0
)

# Check consistency with the previously reported values.
if (
  abs(hpc_lb$p.value - 0.8775) > 0.001 ||
  abs(cpu_lb$p.value - 0.3608) > 0.001
) {
  stop(
    "Ljung-Box p-values differ from the original report. ",
    "Check the saved model versions and test settings."
  )
}

# -------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Prepare data for Q-Q plots
# -------------------------------------------------------

qq_data <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    Resource = "Overall HPC",
    Residual = hpc_residuals
  ),
  data.frame(
    Resource = "CPU",
    Residual = cpu_residuals
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    Resource = factor(
      Resource,
      levels = c("Overall HPC", "CPU")
    )
  )

# -------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Draw the two Q-Q plots
# -------------------------------------------------------

ggplot(
  qq_data,
  aes(sample = Residual)
) +
  stat_qq(
    colour = "#17324D",
    size = 2.0
  ) +
  stat_qq_line(
    colour = "#006DAE",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Resource,
    nrow = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Theoretical normal quantiles",
    y = "Sample residual quantiles"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 13,
      face = "bold",
      colour = "#17324D"
    ),
    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "#EAF3F9",
      colour = NA
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.5, "lines"),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 10, 5, 5)
  )
```

:::

<div class="slide11-diagnostics">

<div class="slide11-diagnostic">
<strong>Overall HPC</strong>
<p>Ljung–Box test (lag 2): <strong>p = `r sprintf("%.4f", hpc_lb$p.value)`</strong></p>
<p>No significant autocorrelation detected at the tested lags; Q–Q tail departures warrant caution.</p>
</div>

<div class="slide11-diagnostic">
<strong>CPU</strong>
<p>Ljung–Box test (lag 2): <strong>p = `r sprintf("%.4f", cpu_lb$p.value)`</strong></p>
<p>No significant autocorrelation detected at the tested lags; Q–Q departures warrant caution.</p>
</div>

</div>

::: {.slide11-caution}
**Diagnostic conclusion:** The Ljung–Box tests found no significant autocorrelation at the tested lags. However, the short historical series and Q–Q departures limit confidence in the assumptions underlying the prediction intervals.
:::

::: {.slide11-note}
**Notes:** Q–Q plots assess residual normality; Ljung–Box tests assess serial correlation. Both diagnostics use residuals from the selected full-history linear models. Non-significant tests do not establish residual independence. Prediction intervals remain conditional on model assumptions. **Methods:** [@HyndmanAthanasopoulos2021]. **Results:** Project model diagnostics.
:::

:::

<div class="slide12-value">
1,369.90 million core-hours
</div>

95% prediction interval: **974.24–1,765.55 million core-hours**.

The central forecast increases by approximately **81.01 million core-hours annually** over 2027–2030.

:::

:::

::: {.slide12-finding}

**Forecast implication:** The selected linear models indicate continued growth in overall HPC and CPU demand through 2030. However, the prediction intervals widen over the forecast horizon, highlighting uncertainty in future requirements. Alternative log-linear scenarios produce substantially higher projections, demonstrating sensitivity to the assumed growth pattern.

:::

::: {.slide12-note}

**Notes:** Annual forecasts and 95% prediction intervals reproduce the project's Chapter 10 scenario forecasting results. The selected models include historical observations through 2026. Prediction intervals are conditional on model assumptions and do not capture all measurement or model uncertainty. Log-linear scenarios are not upper prediction bounds. Panel scales differ. **Source:** Project scenario forecasting analysis, Chapter 10. **Methods:** [@HyndmanAthanasopoulos2021].

:::

:::

```{r}
#| label: slide13-data
#| echo: false
#| include: false

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)

# GPU 2030 scenario results from Chapter 10.
# Units: million GPU-hours.

gpu_2030 <- data.frame(
  scenario = c(
    "Linear excluding 2026",
    "Log-linear excluding 2026",
    "Naïve benchmark",
    "Linear including 2026",
    "Log-linear including 2026"
  ),
  value = c(
    2.25,
    2.41,
    3.00,
    3.37,
    3.68
  )
)

gpu_2030$scenario <- factor(
  gpu_2030$scenario,
  levels = rev(gpu_2030$scenario)
)

gpu_2030$reference <- ifelse(
  gpu_2030$scenario == "Naïve benchmark",
  "Benchmark",
  "Alternative"
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(gpu_2030) == 5,
  all(is.finite(gpu_2030$value)),
  all(gpu_2030$value > 0)
)
```

::: {.slide13}

::: {.slide13-intro}
**Scenario approach:** GPU projections compare alternative growth assumptions using five annual observations (2022–2026). Research-field scenarios apply historical allocation shares to the selected 2030 overall HPC demand projection.

::: {.slide13-explanation}
The **naïve benchmark** achieved the lowest one-step-ahead forecast error, but evaluation covered only **two years**. Trend projections change substantially depending on whether 2026 is included. These scenarios do not establish a reliable single GPU forecast for 2030.
:::

Research-field allocation-share scenarios

::: {.slide13-subtitle}
Illustrative distribution of 2.50 million kSU in 2030
:::

::: {.slide13-table}

| Research field | 2014–20 | 2021–26 | 2030 kSU* |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| Engineering & Technology | 16.24% | 33.28% | 832,000 |
| Earth & Environmental Sciences | 30.38% | 13.36% | 334,000 |
| Physical Sciences | 16.26% | 21.11% | 527,750 |
| Chemical Sciences | 18.28% | 17.02% | 425,500 |

:::

:::

::: {.slide13-explanation}
Applying the **2021–2026 allocation shares**, Engineering & Technology receives the largest illustrative 2030 amount (**832,000 kSU**), followed by Physical Sciences (**527,750 kSU**). These are conditional allocations of the national demand projection, **not independently forecast field-level demand**.
:::

:::

::::

::: {.slide13-bottom}
**Planning implication:** GPU requirements vary substantially across growth assumptions, while research-field allocations depend on the historical reference period selected. More detailed GPU usage and field-level demand data are needed to strengthen projections for national HPC planning.
:::

::: {.slide13-note}
**Notes:** GPU projections are exploratory scenarios, not statistical prediction intervals. The naïve benchmark holds estimated 2026 GPU demand constant. *2030 FoR values apply normalised 2021–2026 allocation shares to the rounded 2.50 million kSU HPC projection. Only four research fields are displayed. Historical comparisons span the ANZSRC 2008/2020 classification change; allocation shares are not direct measures of researcher demand. **Source:** Project scenario forecasting analysis, Chapter 10.
:::

:::

::: {.slide14}

::: {.slide14-headline}
This project establishes a reproducible starting point for national HPC demand forecasting. Stronger planning decisions require integrated and comparable demand data from NCI and Pawsey.
:::

::: {.slide14-grid}

::: {.slide14-colhead}
What the analysis found
:::

::: {.slide14-colhead}
What the Academy can do next
:::

:::

::: {.slide14-pair}

::: {.slide14-cell}
**Overall HPC: 2.50 million kSU by 2030**

Selected linear projection; 95% prediction interval of **1.98–3.03 million kSU**.
:::

::: {.slide14-cell}
**Establish a national planning baseline**

Use the projection and its uncertainty range as an initial scenario, not a fixed infrastructure target.
:::

:::

::: {.slide14-pair}

::: {.slide14-cell}
**CPU: 1.37 billion core-hours by 2030**

Selected linear projection; 95% prediction interval of **0.97–1.77 billion core-hours**.
:::

::: {.slide14-cell}
**Plan CPU requirements separately**

Use CPU core-hours alongside overall HPC service units, recognising differences in resource accounting.
:::

:::

::: {.slide14-pair}

::: {.slide14-cell}
**GPU: Longer-term forecasts remain uncertain**

Only five annual observations; naïve achieved the lowest RMSE in two one-step-ahead evaluations.
:::

::: {.slide14-cell}
**Retain GPU scenarios, not a single target**

Use the naïve benchmark for comparison and refine projections when longer, more detailed GPU records become available.
:::

:::

::: {.slide14-pair}

::: {.slide14-cell}
**FoR: Engineering leads recent allocations**

Engineering & Technology represents **33.28%** and Physical Sciences **21.11%** of 2021–2026 allocation shares.
:::

::: {.slide14-cell}
**Develop research-field demand evidence**

Use allocation shares for illustrative scenarios until consistent, directly observed field-level requests are available.
:::

:::

::: {.slide14-pair}

::: {.slide14-cell}
**Data integration is the critical limitation**

NCI and Pawsey differ in reporting structures, resource units and historical coverage, requiring harmonisation and assumptions.
:::

::: {.slide14-cell}
**Build a consistent national demand dataset**

Standardise units and definitions; distinguish requests, allocations and fulfilment; document conversion rules and data provenance.
:::

:::

::: {.slide14-bottom}
**Recommended next step:** The Academy can use this project's data-integration workflow, forecasting models and scenario framework as a **proof of concept**, working with NCI and Pawsey to refine future national HPC demand estimates as more detailed data become available.
:::

::: {.slide14-note}
**Notes:** HPC and CPU projections use selected linear models including 2026; prediction intervals are conditional on model assumptions. GPU scenarios are exploratory. FoR percentages describe historical allocations, not directly observed demand. Overall HPC service units and CPU core-hours are different accounting measures. **Source:** Project data integration, standardisation and forecasting analyses, Chapters 03–10.
:::
